transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess I’m here because I’ve been feeling a little cloudy in my head lately. Not terrible, I don’t want to make it sound too dramatic, but at work I’ll look at a board packet or a vendor email and just sort of stare at it. Things I used to decide pretty quickly feel harder than they should. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

I don’t know if I’d call it depressed, exactly. Maybe a little low here and there, but nothing too awful. I’ve been trying to keep up and not make a big thing of it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been worrying a lot lately?

Not a lot, I don’t think. I mean, I worry about the usual things, work and getting things done right, but I wouldn’t say it’s taking over or anything. At least, I don’t think so. Is that what you mean?
Did this start after a stressful event or major change in your life?

Maybe, yes. I mean, I don’t want to blame it all on that, but it did seem to start about two weeks ago, around when my husband retired and was suddenly home all day. Since then I’ve felt a sharper change in my energy and confidence, and then this low, cloudy feeling. Does that sound like the kind of change you’re asking about?
Since your husband retired, has having him home all day felt stressful for you?

I’m not sure I’d call it stressful exactly. It’s just… different, having someone there all day when I was used to my own routine. I don’t want to make it sound like he’s done anything wrong. It’s more that I’m still adjusting, I guess. Does that make sense?
Over the past two weeks, have you been feeling sad or down most days?
I’m not sure I’d say sad most days, exactly. I’ve had some low moments, kind of cloudy, but I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Some days I’m okay. Does that answer it?
Have these cloudy feelings made it harder for you to do your work?

A little, yes. I’m still going to work and getting things done, so it’s not like I can’t function. But I’ve been slowing myself down on decisions, and I’ve asked my assistant to double-check vendor details for me. I also put off a couple of board items because I just don’t quite trust my judgment right now. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Since this started, have you been feeling noticeably nervous or on edge?

Some, yes… I don’t want to overstate it. At home I feel more slowed down, like my legs are kind of heavy. But then in meetings, I do notice I’m tapping my pen or shifting around in the chair, like I’m a little too keyed up to just sit still. Is that what you mean by nervous or on edge?
Have you found it hard to stop or control your worrying?
I don’t think so… not in a way I’d call hard to control. I do worry some, but I can usually talk myself through it or move on to the next thing. I’m not sure if that’s what you’re asking.
Over the past two weeks, have you been enjoying your usual activities less than usual?

Yes… I guess I have, a little. I don’t mean I’m just sitting around doing nothing, but I haven’t really wanted to go to my dance class, or stop in at the little galleries like I usually do. And I haven’t felt like cooking Sunday food for my family, which normally makes me feel like myself. Does that count as enjoying things less?
Over the past two weeks, have you had trouble concentrating?

Yes… a bit. I mean, I’m still getting through things, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but my head feels kind of cloudy. I’ll be looking at a board packet or a vendor email, and I just… stare at it longer than I should. Even simple decisions I used to make pretty quickly take me a while now. Is that the kind of concentration trouble you mean?
Over the past two weeks, have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself in some way?

I… I don’t want to worry you. A few mornings, I’ve had this scary thought like maybe it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. But I’m not trying to hurt myself, and I don’t have any plan or anything like that. It just kind of pops into my head, and then I feel bad for even thinking it.
Over the past two weeks, have you been waking up much earlier than usual and unable to get back to sleep?

I don’t think so… not in a way I’ve really noticed. I mean, I wake up sometimes, but I can usually settle back down. It hasn’t been like I’m up at 4 in the morning every day or anything. Is that what you mean?
Over the past two weeks, have you had less appetite than usual?

A little, yes. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but my eating’s been kind of off. I’ll have coffee and just a few bites of something, and that’ll carry me through most of the day. Then at night I might pick at tortillas or something sweet, but I’m not really enjoying it. Does that count as less appetite?
Over the past two weeks, have you been feeling tired or low in energy?

I mean… maybe a little, but I don’t know if I’d call it low energy exactly. I still get myself going and do what I need to do. I just feel kind of worn out here and there. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Over the past two weeks, have these symptoms been happening nearly every day?

Yes… I think so, more or less. It’s been about two weeks now that things have felt different — since my husband retired and suddenly he’s home all day. I don’t want to make too big a deal of it, but that’s when I noticed the shift in my energy and confidence, and then this kind of low, cloudy feeling. So… yes, pretty much most days.
Have these symptoms been causing you significant distress?

I wouldn’t say it’s… terrible, but yes, it’s bothering me. I’m still getting to work and everything, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m falling apart. But I’ve had to slow myself down on decisions, and I’ve asked my assistant to double-check vendor details because I don’t quite trust my judgment right now. I’ve also put off a couple of board items. So… yes, I guess it is causing me some distress.
Do you feel these symptoms are mainly because of adjusting to your husband being home all day since he retired?

I think so, yes… I mean, I don’t want to blame him exactly. But the sharper change in my energy and confidence, and then that low, cloudy feeling, it really started around when he retired and was suddenly home all day. It’s been about two weeks. Does that make sense?
Over the past two weeks, have you been moving or speaking noticeably more slowly than usual?

A little, yes… though I don’t know if it’s obvious to other people. At home I feel like I’m moving slower, like my legs are kind of heavy. But then in meetings it’s almost the opposite — I catch myself tapping my pen or shifting around in the chair, like I’m too keyed up to sit still. I hope that answers what you mean.
Do these feelings seem stronger than you would expect just from adjusting to your husband being home after retirement?

I’m not completely sure how to judge that. Part of me thinks maybe I should be handling it better, since it’s just a change at home. But I don’t know… it does feel a bit bigger than I expected. Not dramatic, but stronger than I would have thought, if that makes sense.
